bump_source: jackson-core 2.15.0 release notes; StreamReadConstraints. The library itself raised maxStringLength from 5M to 20M in 2.15.1 after user reports, which is independent evidence the default bit people -- this project hit it while the cap was still 5M.

behavioral_break.mechanism: jackson-core 2.15.0 introduced StreamReadConstraints with parser limits applied BY DEFAULT: maxStringLength 5,000,000 (raised to 20,000,000 in 2.15.1), maxNestingDepth 1000, maxNumberLength 1000. JSON that 2.14 parsed fine now throws com.fasterxml.jackson.core.exc.StreamConstraintsException at parse time. No signature on the client's path changes, so the client compiles unchanged and fails at run time.
behavioral_break.why_it_breaks: Same as `mechanism`; recorded under both names because older cases in this directory use `why_it_breaks` and newer ones use `mechanism`.
behavioral_break.affected_class: io.json.compare.util.JsonUtils and io.json.compare.matcher.JsonPathMatcher (their two static ObjectMappers)
behavioral_break.observed_exception: com.fasterxml.jackson.core.exc.StreamConstraintsException: String length (5043685) exceeds the maximum length (5000000)
behavioral_break.blast_radius: Every document this library compares. JsonUtils.toJson is the single entry point through which json-compare parses all input, so any user comparing a JSON document with a field above the cap is affected -- which for a comparison library is precisely the payload-inspection use case.

adaptation.repo_note: A JSON comparison library. 77 stars, upstream, not a fork. Single-module Maven.
adaptation.commit_message: Use Integer.MAX_VALUE for ObjectMapper max number, nesting and String length
adaptation.why_that_matters: Integer.MAX_VALUE on all three limits is a full restoration of pre-2.15 behaviour, not a knob parked at the library's own value. There is no configuration surface and no property to set: the limits are simply removed, which is what a library does when a new default breaks its users and it has no way to know how large their documents are.
adaptation.evidence_of_diagnosis: They changed BOTH static ObjectMappers in the same commit -- JsonUtils and JsonPathMatcher -- rather than the one that happened to fail, and recorded the change in Changelog.md. Three days after the crossing, with the commit message naming all three limits.
adaptation.scope: 2 production files plus the changelog; the whole commit is this adaptation and nothing else.

verification.method: Their own Maven build at both commits (mvn -DskipTests package), with the jackson version supplied through THEIR OWN pom properties (-Djackson.version -Djackson.databind.version), so no build file was edited. A driver in the default package calls JsonUtils.toJson(String) -- public, static, no construction needed -- on a JSON document whose single field is 6,000,000 characters, above 2.15.0's 5,000,000 cap. Each state prints the classpath location of the loaded jackson-core jar, so a state cannot silently run the wrong version.
verification.test: JsonCompareBbcDriver.java (authored trigger, THEIR production path). Nothing of theirs is reconstructed: the parse goes through their JsonUtils.MAPPER, the same static mapper their adaptation configures. Only the oversized document and the main() are ours.
verification.why_not_their_own_suite: Their suite passes identically in all three states. JSONLargeCompareTests exists but its fixture sits far below the cap, so no test flips -- no project ships a 6 MB string fixture, which is why this break needs an authored trigger. Their suite does have 3 pre-existing failures on Windows (JsonPrettyPrintlTest, JsonUtilsTest.testEmptyJsonPrettyPrint, MessageUtilTest.testCrop), all line-ending artefacts, and all three fail in EVERY state -- they never enter a baseline-pass set and are unrelated to this break.

states.name: 2_broken
states.result: THREW com.fasterxml.jackson.core.exc.StreamConstraintsException: String length (5043685) exceeds the maximum length (5000000)

verification.isolation: States 2 and 3 resolve the identical jackson-core 2.15.0 jar, so the only variable between them is their own commit. States 1 and 2 share their code exactly, so the only variable is the library version -- and both versions are theirs, from the property Renovate bumped. `mvn clean` runs between states, because incremental compilation would otherwise reuse the previous state's .class files after a checkout.
threats_to_validity: THE TRIGGER IS AUTHORED, not their test, for the reason given in why_not_their_own_suite.

THE EXCEPTION REPORTS 5,043,685 characters rather than the 6,000,000 written. That is jackson's own buffer-boundary accounting -- it aborts as soon as the accumulated segment passes the cap, not after reading the whole field. The number differing from the input is expected, and the cap it names (5,000,000) is exactly 2.15.0's default.
JACKSON-CORE AND -DATABIND were moved together in every state, matching what their pom resolves. Moving core alone would produce a version-skew artefact rather than the break.
